content.overview: Inventory discrepancies and waste workflows must remain reconstructable. The technician preserves evidence and identity instead of hiding mismatches or assuming a universal destruction method.

vocabulary.definition: A difference between expected and observed identity, quantity, status, location or record information.
The authorized decision about what happens to material, such as use, transfer, hold, return or destruction.
The ability to use records to understand what happened to material over time.

sections.title: Investigate without concealing
sections.body: A mismatch may result from counting, delayed entry, wrong identity, unrecorded movement or another control failure. Technicians gather permitted facts, preserve the current state and escalate when the difference cannot be reconciled under procedure.

sections.title: Waste remains identified
sections.body: Material designated as waste remains tied to the identity and quantity information required by the facility and jurisdiction until the authorized waste or destruction workflow is complete. Final disposition may belong to another role.

workedExamples: A waste container lacks a batch identifier, so it is not combined with other waste until identity is resolved.
A system shows destruction complete while the physical material remains; the mismatch is reported rather than ignored.
commonMistakes: Discarding questionable material before identity and status are documented.
Changing records to eliminate an unexplained discrepancy.
content.practicalApplication: Investigate a mock inventory discrepancy and complete a supplied waste/destruction record while identifying which steps require higher authorization.
content.summary: Traceable waste handling requires preserved identity, honest discrepancy records and local authorization for disposition or destruction.

blocks.title: Waste does not stop being controlled material just because it will be discarded
blocks.body: A waste or destruction workflow should remain connected to the source material and the controlled event history until the applicable facility and jurisdiction process is complete. This course teaches reconstructable identity and documentation; it does not impose one universal cannabis destruction method or platform workflow.

blocks.title: Keep a waste or destruction event reconstructable

items.title: Confirm source identity
items.body: Tie the material to the controlled plant, batch, lot, container, room, or other source identity required by the facility process.

items.title: Preserve quantity or count context
items.body: Capture the required weight, count, volume, or other measure when the applicable workflow requires it.

items.title: Preserve status before disposition
items.body: Keep the material identified and separated as required until the authorized decision and workflow occur.

items.title: Record the approved event
items.body: Document the applicable method, time, location, responsible roles, witnesses, or other fields required by the controlling local process.

items.title: Record final disposition
items.body: The record should show what ultimately happened to the material without inventing steps that belong to another role or jurisdiction.

left.label: Traceable
left.body: A waste container remains linked to its source material, required quantity information, status, authorized disposition event, and final record until the workflow is complete.

right.label: Untraceable
right.body: Questionable material is discarded or mixed into a general waste container before its identity and status are resolved, destroying the evidence needed to reconstruct what happened.

blocks.title: A waste container has no source identifier
blocks.setting: A container marked as cultivation waste is staged for the next disposal step, but the source batch or material identity cannot be confirmed. Another identified waste container is beside it.
blocks.prompt: What should the technician do first?
options: Combine the containers because both are waste
Estimate the missing identity from the room location
Keep the unidentified material separate, preserve its current state, and escalate the identity problem under procedure before combining or disposing it
Discard the unidentified container immediately so it cannot be confused with good material
blocks.answer: Keep the unidentified material separate, preserve its current state, and escalate the identity problem under procedure before combining or disposing it.
blocks.feedback: Disposal intent does not remove the need for reconstructable identity and status. Combining or discarding the material can erase the evidence needed to resolve the discrepancy.

blocks.title: Vendor-neutral waste / disposition record anatomy
blocks.description: Exact required fields are facility- and jurisdiction-specific. These fields illustrate the stable traceability questions a controlled waste event may need to answer.

fields.label: Source identity
fields.value: Plant, batch, lot, container, room, or other controlled source

fields.label: Material description
fields.value: What material entered the waste/disposition workflow

fields.label: Status / reason
fields.value: Why the material is held for waste, return, destruction, or other disposition

fields.label: Authorized event
fields.value: The local approved disposition/destruction step or decision

fields.label: Time / location
fields.value: When and where the event occurred

fields.label: Responsible roles
fields.value: Required operator, approver, witness, or system attribution where applicable

fields.label: Final disposition
fields.value: What ultimately happened to the identified material

blocks.note: Use the actual facility and jurisdiction process for required fields, approvals, methods, witnesses, and system entries.

blocks.title: Audit a discrepancy and waste packet
blocks.instructions: Review a mock record set containing one unresolved inventory mismatch, one identified waste container, one unidentified waste container, and one system entry that reports disposition before the physical event occurred.
prompts: Separate confirmed facts from possible causes.
Identify which material must remain separate until identity is resolved.
Identify which actions a Technician I worker may document versus which disposition decisions require another role.
Produce a reconstructable handoff without inventing a jurisdiction-specific destruction rule.

blocks.title: Key takeaway
blocks.body: A material discrepancy is not solved by throwing material away or editing the record. Preserve identity and physical state, document what is known, and let the authorized local process determine disposition or destruction.
